articles.title: ‘When you tell people the story, it’s almost too good to be true’: the incredible journey behind The Cycle of Love
articles.summary: Documentary director Orlando von Einsiedel on how the real life tale of a man who cycles 6,000 miles from India to Sweden to find his true love will warm your heart. New Delhi, December 1975.
body: New Delhi, December 1975. It was love at first sight when a Swedish hippy called Lotta von Schedvin sat down to be sketched by an Indian street artist, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia, known to everyone as PK. In the 10 minutes it took PK to complete her portrait, everything clicked into place for the pair. They were swept headlong in a whirlwind romance, and PK took Lotta to his village in the east of India to meet his family. But soon after, the time came for Lotta to pack up her VW campervan and head back home with her friends.

Heart-stricken PK promised to follow, but a plane ticket to Sweden was an impossible dream. Determined not to lose the love of his life, PK bought a secondhand Raleigh bike, and with $80 sewn into the waistband of his trousers, set off to cycle 6,000 miles to Lotta. He knew the sun set in the west, so that was the direction he took. His plan was to follow the hippy trail, cycling through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran and Turkey, crossing Europe, finally arriving in Sweden.
points: Documentary director Orlando von Einsiedel on how the real life tale of a man who cycles 6,000 miles from India to Sweden to find his true love will warm your heart.

articles.title: ‘I thank God for killing me and bringing me back’: Nicolas Winding Refn on the emergency op that inspired his new sci-fi horror
articles.summary: Notorious for ultra-violent movies like Drive and The Neon Demon, the Dane had lost the will to direct until ‘the Tom Cruise of surgeons’ saved his life – and triggered an astonishing creative rebirth.
body: Nicolas Winding Refn has his phone out, showing me one of the goriest scenes he’s ever been involved in. Given that the Danish director’s movies have involved hands getting sliced off, eyeballs being gouged out and a son reaching deep inside his mother’s womb, that’s certainly saying something. In this video, the camera is fixed upon a beating heart when suddenly – slash! – it gets sliced open with a knife. We travel into the open chamber, as needles arrive to pierce through the muscle. Unsettling and compelling, could this be a future Palme d’Or winner?

Sitting in a swanky London hotel bar, drinking espressos and wearing a smart blue polo shirt under a skinny suit, Refn is here to talk about his latest movie, Her Private Hell, a ludicrously camp dream-collage of sci-fi, horror, spoof and revenge set in neon-lit Tokyo. But for the first 40 minutes of our chat, he recounts – with precious little interruption from me – the story of the 2023 operation that saved his life. Without it, he says, Her Private Hell would never have been made – not so much on health grounds, but because, before he was given this second chance at life, he had lost the passion for making movies.

articles.title: ‘Avengers’ Studio AGBO’s Chris Brearton, Dominic Hughes to Keynote Tokyo Market on Artist-Led AI in Storytelling
articles.summary: TIFFCOM, the content market held in coordination with the Tokyo International Film Festival, will host a keynote presentation by Chris Brearton and Dominic Hughes, partner and chief scientific Officer, respectively, of AGBO, the studio founded by Anthony and Joe Russo.
body: Before joining AGBO, Brearton was VP of corporate strategy at Amazon MGM Studios, where he oversaw the integration of MGM into Amazon. Hughes, a leader in algorithms, machine learning and AI, partners with AGBO’s storytelling and innovation teams to guide the development and deployment of AI technologies within the creative process.

The Russo Brothers and AGBO have generated more than $7 billion at the global box office and produced 17 No. 1 worldwide debuts, including “ Avengers: Endgame.” The studio is currently in post-production on “Avengers: Doomsday,” set for release Dec. 18.

The keynote leads TIFFCOM’s second wave of confirmed conferences. The Association of Japanese Animations will present a special session on “Japanese Animation’s Global Expansion” on Oct. 30, unveiling the first public data from its 2025 industry survey alongside overseas strategy presentations from Nippon Animation and Production I.G. Speakers include Nippon Animation international sales director Hitomi Hiratsuka and Production I.G. corporate administration and IP director Yoko Ueda, with opening remarks from Association of Japanese Animations president Kazuko Ishikawa.

articles.title: ‘Jujutsu Kaisen’ Vaults MAPPA to Anime Studio Lead as Streaming Shifts From Licensing to Ownership, Media Partners Asia Report Finds
articles.summary: Anime drew a larger monthly audience than any other genre on Asian streaming platforms between July 2025 and August 2026, and viewing on Netflix grew nine times faster than the service overall, according to a new report from Media Partners Asia (MPA).
body: Netflix carried roughly half of the region’s anime viewing across the tracking period, holding 51% of anime hours in the second half of 2025 and 50% in the first half of 2026. Japan, the world’s largest anime market, has become a two-way contest between the two biggest global platforms: Prime Video held a 43% share of anime hours there in the second half of 2025, before Netflix pulled even with 42% each in the first half of 2026.

MPA’s classification of Netflix’s “What We Watched” disclosures shows the platform’s Japanese anime viewing climbing from 3.33 billion hours in the first half of 2023 to 4.64 billion hours in the first half of 2026, a 39% jump against 4.5% growth in Netflix’s total viewing over the same period. Anime rose from 3.6% to 4.75% of all Netflix hours in that window. Four-fifths of that viewing remains licensed library content, though MPA points to Netflix’s January 2026 partnership with MAPPA as a marker of the shift toward owned franchises.

articles.title: Eddie Cahyono’s Busan Competition Title ‘Ibuku,’ Starring Christine Hakim, Boarded by Asian Shadows for World Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Asian Shadows has boarded international sales rights to Eddie Cahyono’s “Ibuku,” starring Christine Hakim and Ayushita Nugraha, which the Busan International Film Festival has selected for its Competition lineup.
body: Hakim’s credits span five decades and include “Tjoet Nja’ Dhien,” “Eat Pray Love” and HBO’s “The Last of Us.” Nugraha has appeared in “What They Don’t Talk About When They Talk About Love” and “Kartini: Princess of Java,” while Simatupang’s film work includes “Gie,” “Soegija” and “Kartini: Princess of Java.”

Indonesia’s ANP Talenta Media, run by Tika Bravani, and Japan’s Knockonwood Inc., headed by Shin Yamaguchi, are producing “Ibuku,” with Hong Kong’s Chinese Shadows executives Isabelle Glachant and Li Xiaorong on board as creative producers. Cahyono holds an executive producer credit via his own Memorieslight Pictures. The film is Bravani’s first as a feature producer.

“‘Ibuku’ is a poetic and touching portrait of a mother through the timeless eyes of her own daughter,” said Maria Ruggieri, Asian Shadows’ head of sales and acquisitions. “We are proud to bring Ibuku to the attention of the International audience.”

articles.title: The Watergate Caper: Richard Nixon and the Death of the American Dream review – political scandal, 70s style
articles.summary: Shane O’Sullivan’s documentary weaves archive clips and snippets from films old and new to draw out the highlights of the crisis that rocked the US. Judging by his past work, the Irish-born, London-based writer and film-maker Shane O’Sullivan may have a chronic case of born-too-late nostalgia.
body: Alongside this, the archive material is neatly marshalled and excerpted in such a way as to explain to a bright gen Alpha kid roughly what this Watergate thing was all about, although O’Sullivan chooses not to get to bogged down in the detail and mostly surveys the highlights. Of particular note are some less well-known clips of “Tricky Dicky” Nixon himself, coming across as surprisingly amusing, joking around with his aides before the cameras go live. Even when we see him lying through his teeth, one can’t help thinking he seems like Abraham Lincoln compared with the current occupant of the White House. The times, they have a-changed, and not for the better.

articles.title: Zhang Yimou to Lead Busan Competition Jury
articles.summary: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has confirmed seven jurors for its Competition section, with Chinese director Zhang Yimou serving as jury president for the section’s second edition.
body: The jury will evaluate 13 films in this year’s Competition lineup. The Busan Award, presented across five categories, best film, best director, special jury prize, best actor and artistic contribution, carries total prize money of KRW110 million($80,350). Following BIFF’s recognition this year as a FIAPF A-list festival, alongside Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance and Toronto, the best film winner now also qualifies directly for the best international feature film category at the Academy Awards.
The 31st Busan International Film Festival will Oct. 6-15, at the Busan Cinema Center and throughout Busan, with the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13.

articles.title: Stadium owner Robert Kraft says Ed Sheeran asked him to donate $2m in aid after Macklemore backlash
articles.summary: It comes after Macklemore pledged $1m to Palestinian causes, challenging the tycoon to match the sum.
body: Robert Kraft, the US stadium owner who had pro-Palestinian rapper Macklemore removed as Ed Sheeran's opening act, says Sheeran asked him to match his own $2m (£1.5m) donation for "aid in the region".
It came after Macklemore said he would donate $1m (£750,000) to Palestinian organisations, challenging Kraft to match him.

Kraft, who owns the New England Patriots, wrote on Wednesday: "Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis.
"Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges."

articles.title: Palace in war of words with Earl Spencer over claims in Diana book
articles.summary: The row threatens to overshadow a very crowded day for the royals - with the King and Princes William and Harry all attending events.
body: Buckingham Palace is in a war of words with Earl Spencer, the brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, over a controversial memoir about her life and death.
King Charles is accused of insensitively saying to Earl Spencer, in the wake of Diana's death in 1997, that "we'll forget her soon enough", according to excerpts published in the Daily Mail.
But the Palace has pushed back unusually strongly, angered by the claims and attempting to cast doubt on them.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss," it said.

articles.title: King Charles Makes Rare Statement Over Bombshell Memoir Claim He Told Diana’s Brother: “We’ll Forget Her Soon Enough”
articles.summary: The Royal Family has, as the British press says, been dragged into a war of words with Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the beloved Princess Diana.
body: King Charles has, as the British press put it, been dragged into a “war of words” this week with Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the late Princess Diana.
Ahead of the release of Earl Spencer’s bombshell memoir about his sibling next week, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, one particular claim from the book has seemingly thrown the Palace for a loop.

Such is the backlash that the Palace has made a rare public statement over the matter, where the firm appears to cast doubt on Spencer’s recollection of the event: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss,” it said, per BBC News.

The language, reporters have pointed out, is strikingly similar to Queen Elizabeth’s response to allegations of racism from Prince Harry and Meghan Markle in 2021, when she stated “recollections may vary,” in what was a surprisingly firm response from the monarch.
points: The Royal Family has, as the British press says, been dragged into a war of words with Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the beloved Princess Diana.
